title: 3D printing
summary: 3D printing, also called additive manufacturing, constructs three-dimensional objects from digital models by depositing material layer by layer under computer control. While originally limited to prototyping, modern processes can produce complex geometries with internal structures, reduced waste, and varied materials including thermoplastics and powders. The technology has evolved from experimental methods in the 1980s to a viable industrial-production technology as of 2019.

mechanisms.title: Layer-by-layer material deposition
mechanisms.explanation: Material is deposited, joined, or solidified under computer control, typically adding material together in the form of plastics, liquids, or powder grains fused layer by layer to build the object.

mechanisms.title: Computer numerical control of deposition
mechanisms.explanation: The printing process is governed by computer numerical control, guiding the precise placement of material based on a CAD or digital 3D model to shape the object.
